messages:
sam: hitting intermittent JSONDecodeError when parsing SSE chunks in our Python client (uvloop + aiohttp). looks like chunk boundaries sometimes split a single JSON payload across two chunks. repro attached.
neha: can you paste the read loop? maybe we're not respecting SSE framing (\n\n) or mis-handling keepalives.
sam: here's the simplified loop:

```
async for chunk in resp.content.iter_chunked(1024):
    buf += chunk.decode()
    while '\n\n' in buf:
        event, buf = buf.split('\n\n', 1)
        if event.startswith('data: '):
            payload = event[len('data: '):]
            obj = json.loads(payload)  # JSONDecodeError on partial
```

taylor: yep that's the classic partial-frame problem. two quick options: 1) keep doing the buffer approach but use incremental parsing (JSONDecoder.raw_decode) to parse prefix and get consumed length; 2) switch to an actual SSE parser that yields complete events (and handle :keepalive lines).
neha: raw_decode example? that sounds promising if you want to stick to stdlib.
sam: sth like this worked for me locally:

```
from json import JSONDecoder
decoder = JSONDecoder()

# inside loop after you have 'payload' string that might include extra bytes
idx = 0
while idx < len(payload):
    try:
        obj, consumed = decoder.raw_decode(payload[idx:])
        idx += consumed
        handle_obj(obj)
    except ValueError:
        # incomplete json -> break and wait for more data
        break
# leftover = payload[idx:]
```

neha: nice. also consider moving parsing into a dedicated parser task and use an asyncio.Queue(maxsize=256) between the reader and parser to provide backpressure. if queue.put blocks (await), that slows the reader and prevents unbounded memory growth.
taylor: +1. something like:

```
q = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=256)
# reader
await q.put(raw_event)
# parser worker
item = await q.get()
```

sam: good call. we're seeing CPU spikes when many clients connect; queue throttling should help.
neha: also check your resp.content.iter_chunked size. uvloop may coalesce TCP frames; smaller chunk size doesn't guarantee event boundaries. rely on SSE framing (\n\n) and incremental parse, not chunk boundaries.
taylor: one more gotcha: token refresh race. if a background refresh updates headers while the stream is mid-read, you can see transient 401s and reconnect storms. use a refresh lock and update the session header before reconnecting the stream.

sam: that was happening too — we had multiple tasks trying to refresh same token. added an asyncio.Lock around refresh and it cleaned up the reconnect noise.

neha: @sam can you upload a tiny repro test that CI can run? if flaky we should add retry logic in the test harness or use deterministic fake socket.
sam: will push a repro in a few mins. also adding a small integration test that simulates split JSON across SSE events and verifies decoder.raw_decode recovers.

taylor: for perf, ijson (yajl backend) is faster for huge streams but for small events raw_decode is fine and simpler.
neha: summary action items: sam -> push repro + fix branch (raw_decode + queue backpressure), taylor -> write token-refresh lock helper, neha -> add CI test wrapper to reduce flakiness. tagging for review: @neha @taylor :eyes:
